jin: Quick heads-up — I spun up marmoset_v1 in staging with int8 per-channel quant to sanity-check onboarding. Ran wiki holdout recall@10 and saw drop ~3.0% vs float32. Anyone else seeing this?
ellie: I ran a tiny sweep yesterday, saw ~2.6% drop on short queries but cluster purity (silhouette) looked fine.
sam: can you paste the eval snippet/command?
jin: sure — command and trimmed output:```bash
./tools/eval_embeddings --model marmoset_v1 --quant int8_perchannel --holdout wiki --k 10 --norm l2
# results (k=10):
# float32 baseline recall@10: 0.842
# int8_perchannel recall@10: 0.812
# delta: -0.030
```
arjun: thanks — do you have per-cohort breakdowns? long-tail vs short-tail?
jin: short-tail (top decile freq) delta was -0.01, long-tail delta -0.05. So effect is concentrated on rare items.
maya: interesting. did you apply post-quant whitening / mean-centering?
jin: no whitening in that run. I tried with batch whitening and saw recall@10 go to 0.826 for int8 (delta -0.016).
ellie: small improvement with whitening lines up with previous models. What about using per-tensor int8 vs per-channel?
sam: per-tensor usually cheaper but noisier. we should try int8_pertensor symmetric and asymmetric to compare.
jin: queued a 3x run: int8_perchannel, int8_pertensor_symmetric, int8_pertensor_asymmetric. also toggling l2 norm vs none.
ops-bot: deploy-staging: marmoset_v1 int8_perchannel finished in 12m.
jin: ran clustering quick-check with UMAP+HDBSCAN — cluster counts similar but some tail clusters merged. snippet:```python
# umap params
mapper = UMAP(n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, metric='cosine')
clusters = HDBSCAN(min_cluster_size=10).fit_predict(mapper.fit_transform(vecs))
```
arjun: merged tail clusters could explain recall loss for rare items. maybe quantization shrinks vector variance in low-frequency tokens.
maya: can we try a small calibration pass: compute per-dataset scale factors on float embeddings and apply to quantized vectors (gain correction)?
jin: good idea — implemented quick scale-correction: scale = mean_norm_float / mean_norm_quant. applying scale recovered ~60% of delta (recall@10 -> 0.832).
ellie: promising. does that affect cosine vs dot-prod ranking differently?
jin: dot-prod ranking improved more than cosine — likely because scaling changes norms; after l2 norm the difference disappears.
sam: operational note — calibration adds negligible CPU at embed time but complicates runtime path. we should weigh engineering cost vs quality.
arjun: also validate with KNN precision@k and mean reciprocal rank. recall alone can hide re-rank flips.
jin: addedMRR: float32 0.64, int8 0.59, int8+calib 0.62.
maya: can you push the evaluation artifacts (UMAP PDFs, topk diffs) to the share?
jin: uploaded to /shared/emb-ops/marmoset/2026-03-23/ — filenames: umap_tail_merge.pdf, recall_table.csv, topk_diff_samples.jsonl
sam: let's run a sanity A/B in staging traffic with fallback: use int8 by default, float32 for requests flagged as high-risk (long queries / low-frequency ids). We can route by policy in redwood-optimize.
arjun: also test per-channel quant with narrow calibration (only scale nonzero dims) vs global scale.
ellie: schedule a short lab session tomorrow to pick best config. propose: 1) int8_perchannel + whitening + calibration, 2) int8_pertensor_asym + l2 norm, 3) float32 fallback policy. measure recall@1/5/10, MRR, silhouette, and tail cluster count.
jin: created ticket RNW-ops-1247 with links and configs. Will run the three configs and post results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
maya: llgtm
ops-bot: reminder: nightly-smoke will re-run these tests at 03:00 UTC.
